transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-05-09
Start: 11:00 AM PDT (15:00:00Z)
Duration: 52m
Location: Zoom
Agenda: marketplace packaging, VPC/KMS compatibility, quantization and perf tradeoffs, pilot benchmarking plan
Attendees: Laura (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Solutions), Omar (Redwood Product), Aisha (Sundial Rails Head of Cloud), Benji (Platform), Ruth (Security), Tom (Product), Evan (SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync to align on Sundial Rails marketplace listing readiness, surface KMS/VPC networking constraints, and agree on a lightweight benchmark for throughput and latency. Action items and next steps captured at the end.

[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, uh, quick intros please — I'm Laura, AE on the Redwood side. Miguel, Priya, Omar with me.
[00:12] Aisha Mohammed: Hi all, Aisha here, I'll be owning the integration at Sundial. We've got Benji, Ruth, Tom and Evan joining.
[00:21] Miguel Torres: Cool, thanks. Today we want to cover packaging requirements for the marketplace listing, network/KMS constraints you mentioned in the pre-call, and then go into perf tradeoffs — quantization vs latency. Sound right?
[00:32] Benji Park: That's correct. We are prioritizing a listing that can be installed into our gov and prod clusters. Key constraints: private VPC peering only, HSM-backed KMS in our AWS account, and minimal egress.
[00:47] Ruth Delgado: And from security we'll need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, SSO via SAML, RBAC mapping, and retention controls.
[00:56] Priya Nair: Great, we'll map that out. Quick question — for the marketplace package, do you expect us to provide a helm chart + operator or do you prefer a simpler helm-only?
[01:07] Tom Nguyen: Prefer helm-only initially, we want a fast install, but need lifecycle hooks to rotate keys and upgrade model versions cleanly.
[01:17] Omar Khatib: Noted. Our recommended pattern is helm chart with an optional operator for larger fleets; helm-only will work for pilot. We'll provide sample values for VPC endpoints and KMS integration.
[01:27] Evan Li: On the KMS piece, our HSM requires a specific key policy — can Redwood call into our KMS from within the cluster, or do you require a control-plane handshake?
[01:38] Miguel Torres: Two options: 1) Redwood Private (control plane in-customer) where the inference runtime runs entirely in your VPC and uses your KMS directly, or 2) Marketplace listing where the runtime runs in-customer but some telemetry to Redwood control plane is optional. For HSM we recommend Private or a hybrid with approved client certs.
[01:55] Aisha Mohammed: So are there any functions unavailable in helm-only deploys? Does streaming or model hot swapping work?
[02:04] Miguel Torres: Streaming works, KV cache and model hot swap are supported but require ephemeral storage and a bit of extra config. We can show a sample values file for model pinning and cache mounts.
[02:16] Benji Park: Perf — what's the typical p95 for a 4k context on an A10055-ish class node? (laughs) we don't actually have A10055 — sorry, my bad.
[02:29] Miguel Torres: (chuckle) common. On Nvidia A100 80GB we see sub-200ms p95 for gpt-ish 2.7B opt models at batch size 1 in our hosted tests; larger contexts and quantized weights change that. With int8 quant and runtime kernels we get cost wins but p95 can rise 10–30ms depending on decoding.
[02:48] Tom Nguyen: We're obviously balancing cost vs latency. For user-facing chat we need p95 < 250ms. For background summarization higher latency is acceptable.
[02:57] Priya Nair: That's a helpful split — we typically recommend routing policies: low-latency traffic to dedicated capacity, background to cheaper quantized variants.
[03:09] Ruth Delgado: About audit logs — can we configure audit retention locally? compliance wants 1 year retention and an export path.
[03:17] Laura Chen: Yes, audit logs can be stored in-cluster and shipped to your SIEM; we'll include fluentd configuration in the helm values. The control plane also keeps an obfuscated activity log for rollouts if you opt into telemetry.
[03:30] Benji Park: For connectivity there is a strict egress policy — are there any third-party endpoints the runtime hits out of the box?
[03:38] Miguel Torres: No hard-coded external calls except optional metrics/health probes. For marketplace install we can default telemetry off. If you want to enable Redwood console features we can set up a push via your outbound-only proxy.
[03:52] Evan Li: Benchmarks — what would you recommend we run locally to validate throughput?
[03:58] Miguel Torres: We'll provide a small harness: sample prompts, concurrency profiles, and token distributions. Run a 48-hour soak at steady QPS and a burst test. We'll also give a quick script to collect p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization.
[04:12] Aisha Mohammed: Excellent. On model licensing and cataloging — we need to ensure the marketplace listing indicates model provenance and allowed usage. Any special fields we should include?
[04:23] Omar Khatib: Include model family, weights source, license (e.g., Apache/MIT/Custom), recommended quantization profile, and supported sequence lengths. We'll add a sample metadata.yaml for the listing.
[04:34] Benji Park: What about automatic fallback? If the quantized variant fails quality checks, can traffic route to a higher-fidelity copy?
[04:42] Miguel Torres: Yes — Redwood's rollout layer supports canary and automatic fallback to pinned model variants. We'll show routing policy snippets in the values file.
[04:52] Tom Nguyen: Security again — SAML integration mapping groups to RBAC. Do you support SCIM?
[04:58] Priya Nair: For Private deployments you'll manage SAML/SCIM; for marketplace installs we support SAML SSO and can wire up group mapping via claims. We'll include an example.
[05:10] Ruth Delgado: Any prerequisites for the helm install regarding CSI drivers or kernel modules for GPU passthrough?
[05:18] Miguel Torres: You need nvidia-device-plugin for Kubernetes and a CSI for your chosen volume (we recommend nv-journal or similar for small KV caching). We'll include a quick preflight checklist in the repo.
[05:29] Benji Park: Okay good. Competitors — quick question, how do you compare to AetherML? Their marketplace seems to auto-provide operator-managed upgrades.
[05:37] Laura Chen: AetherML's approach is operator-centric; Redwood emphasizes a dev-friendly helm pattern with optional operator and more deterministic performance controls for inference economics — caching, batching, routing. We'll share a short comparison doc.
[05:50] Aisha Mohammed: Great. Let's talk timeline — we want to be ready for a limited internal pilot in 3 weeks. Realistic?
[05:57] Miguel Torres: Yes, if we provide the packaging checklist and you run the 48-hour benchmark next week we can iterate on any KMS issues. So two to three weeks is feasible.
[06:07] Tom Nguyen: For the benchmark, can Redwood provide expected pass/fail thresholds?
[06:12] Miguel Torres: We'll suggest throughput targets, latency SLOs (p95 thresholds), and CPU/GPU utilization targets. For pilot, hit p95 < 250ms for chat path and less than 70% GPU avg utilization at target QPS.
[06:28] Evan Li: One more — log forwarding volume. Our SIEM ingestion costs scale, so we'd like a config to sample or batched-forward logs.
[06:37] Priya Nair: We'll include sampling configs and a buffer option so logs can be batched before shipping.
[06:45] Benji Park: Anything else on pricing — do we need an estimate for Dedicated capacity?
[06:50] Laura Chen: We'll follow up with a committed capacity estimate and a marketplace-per-seat baseline for early pilot.
[06:58] Aisha Mohammed: Okay let's recap next steps.
[07:02] Laura Chen: Recap: Redwood sends packaging checklist + helm example, benchmark harness, and comparison doc; Sundial runs 48-hour benchmark and shares telemetry; Sundial security shares exact KMS policy docs; agree to a follow-up KMS integration week of May 20th.
[07:18] Tom Nguyen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:21] Miguel Torres: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
